about.title: About the maker
about.portraitAlt: Julija on a bench against a deep red wall, in a black leather jacket
about.body:
I believe there is no second person quite like you. A piece of jewellery is my way of saying that out loud — not to decorate, but to name something that belongs to the one who wears it. That is why I work mostly to commission, one piece at a time.

My philosophy of life is set into every piece. I cannot put it into words — but I can put it into the work.

Meaning and form I look for in nature: the way a branch grows, the way a fold falls, the way a stone holds its colour. Nature never repeats itself — and in that we are alike.

For five years I have been studying the craft at Oleg Auzer’s jewellery school in Old Riga, where the workshop, the Museum of Living Silver and the hall he lectures in all sit under one roof: you learn not only the techniques, but a way of looking at metal. For eight years I have also been studying psychology and philosophy — they give me that other angle, where you begin to notice what you used to walk past.

My first degree is in law, a master’s from Daugavpils University, followed by years in management. I live and work in Riga.

Everything I manage to make I owe to my teachers and mentors. This is my lasting gratitude to them.

steps.title: Idea and sketch
steps.text: Every piece starts on paper — proportion, weight and the way it will sit on the body.

steps.title: Metal
steps.text: Sterling silver and gold, worked by hand: sawing, forging, soldering, filing.

steps.title: Stone
steps.text: Stones are chosen one by one and set to suit the character of the metal.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Polishing, patina and a final check — each piece exists in a single copy.
